summary: Eduard Sievers was a linguist who studied at Leipzig and Berlin under Georg Curtius, August Leskien, and Friedrich Zarncke. He held professorships at the universities of Jena (1871–1883), Tübingen (1883–1887), Halle-Wittenberg (1887–1892), and Leipzig (1892–1922).

Eduardo Francisco Freyre Roach is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Buddhist Studies at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2014) under the supervision of Yakupitiyage Karunadasa and Georgios T. Halkias.

Edvard Westermarck worked in philosophy and religious studies, having studied at the University of Helsinki (~1881–1889). He held academic posts at the London School of Economics (~1904–1930) and Åbo Akademi University (~1918–1932).

Edward Albert Gait was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at University College London (~1880–1882). He founded the Bihar and Orissa Research Society in 1914 and served as its president from 1915 to 1920.

Edward Backhouse Eastwick worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Charterhouse, Merton College, and Oxford, he was Professor of Hindustani and Telugu at East India Company College (1845) and served in the Foreign Office (~1860–1863).

Edward Byles Cowell, an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and Iranian/Central Asian specialist, studied at Oxford under Horace Hayman Wilson. He held posts at Presidency University, University of Calcutta, and Sanskrit College, later serving as Professor of Sanskrit at Cambridge (1867–1903).

Edward C. Dimock Jr. was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Harvard and Yale. He taught linguistics and Asian languages at the University of Chicago (1966–1993) and served as president of the American Institute of Indian Studies (1972–1986).

Edward Capps was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics who studied at Illinois College, Yale, Berlin, Munich, and Halle-Wittenberg. He held posts at Illinois College (1887–1888), Yale University (1890–1907), and Princeton University (1907–1936).

Edward Clive Bayley was an Indology and history/archaeology specialist who studied at East India Company College (~1840–1842) and Haileybury and Imperial Service College. He joined the Indian Civil Service in 1842.

Edward Conze was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned his Ph.D. at Cologne under Max Scheler, also studying under Max Walleser. He held posts at London, Wisconsin-Madison, Washington, UC Berkeley, Lancaster, and the Buddhist Society.

Edward Delavan Perry was a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied at Columbia University (~1871–1875) and the University of Tübingen (~1877–1879). He served as Jay Professor of Greek and Latin at Columbia University from 1891 to 1931.

Edward Denison Ross was a linguist and Iranian/Central Asian scholar who studied at UCL and under Theodor Nöldeke at Strasbourg. He held posts at UCL, Aliah University, the National Archives of India, the British Museum, and directed SOAS (1916–1937).

Edward Elbridge Salisbury was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Yale and in Europe under Woolsey, Silvestre de Sacy, Garcin de Tassy, Bopp, Lassen, and Burnouf. He was Professor of Arabic and Sanskrit at Yale (1841–1854).

Edward Evan Evans-Pritchard was a religious studies scholar who studied at Oxford and the London School of Economics. He held posts at the London School of Economics (~1928–1930), Cairo University (~1930–1932), Cambridge (~1945–1946), and Oxford (1946–1970).

Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology who completed his doctoral studies under Roderick S. Bucknell (attested 1994) and held a post at the University of Sydney.

Edward Garrett is a linguist and Tibetologist who completed his Ph.D. at UCLA under Carson T. Schütze and Dominique Sportiche, mentored postdoctorally by Anna Szabolcsi. He held research assistant posts at UCLA (1996–2000) and the University of Virginia (2000–2001).

Edward Granville Browne was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar and linguist who studied at Cambridge under William Wright and Edward Byles Cowell. He was a lecturer in Persian (1888) and Adams Professor of Arabic (1902) at Cambridge.

Edward H. Schafer was a sinologist who studied at UCLA, UC Berkeley, the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and Harvard. He was a faculty member in the Department of Oriental Languages at UC Berkeley from ~1947 to 1984.

Edward Hamilton Johnston was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Oxford under Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1909–1924) and was later Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (~1937–1942).

Edward James Rapson, an Indologist, linguist, and historian/archaeologist, studied at St John's College, Cambridge. He worked at the British Museum's Coin Room (1887–1906) and was Professor of Sanskrit at University College London (1903) and Cambridge (1906–1936).
